comment: Curated seed of key Holocaust / WWII events. Claude matches a person's known places and dates against these to weave historical context into the timeline and suggest relevant archives. Seeded in part from the Mémorial de la Shoah key-dates resource. This is a starting set and is meant to be expanded.

events.title: Hitler appointed Chancellor
events.description: Adolf Hitler becomes Chancellor of Germany; the Nazi regime begins.

events.title: Jewish emigration before the war
events.description: As persecution intensified, roughly half of Germany's Jews emigrated. Many sought refuge in France, Britain, Palestine, and the Americas — leaving immigration, visa, and naturalization records abroad.

events.title: Nuremberg Race Laws
events.description: Laws stripping German Jews of citizenship and prohibiting marriage with non-Jews.

events.title: Kristallnacht ('Night of Broken Glass')
events.description: Coordinated pogrom against Jews; synagogues burned, businesses destroyed, ~30,000 Jewish men arrested and sent to camps.

events.title: Kindertransport
events.description: Britain admitted roughly 10,000 mostly Jewish children from Germany, Austria, and Czechoslovakia in the months before the war. A common path by which a family line survived — leaving UK arrival and refugee records.

events.title: Voyage of the MS St. Louis
events.description: A ship of over 900 Jewish refugees was turned away from Cuba and the US and forced back to Europe — emblematic of the closing of refuge before the war.

events.title: Germany invades Poland — WWII begins
events.description: The invasion of Poland begins the Second World War in Europe and the persecution of Polish Jewry.

events.title: Germany invades France and the Low Countries
events.description: Invasion of France, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg.

events.title: Auschwitz concentration camp established
events.description: The Auschwitz camp opens; it would grow into the largest Nazi camp complex and a center of mass murder.

events.title: Fall of France; Vichy regime established
events.description: France signs an armistice; the collaborationist Vichy government soon enacts anti-Jewish laws.

events.title: Warsaw Ghetto sealed
events.description: The largest ghetto in occupied Europe is sealed off; Łódź and other ghettos were established around this period.

events.title: Operation Barbarossa
events.description: Germany invades the USSR; mass shootings of Jews by Einsatzgruppen begin in occupied Soviet territories.

events.title: Drancy internment camp opens
events.description: Drancy becomes the main transit camp for Jews deported from France; ~63,000 of the ~76,000 Jews deported from France passed through it, mostly to Auschwitz.

events.title: Kamenets-Podolsk massacre
events.description: About 23,600 Jews were murdered, including many deported from Hungarian-held territory — an early instance of mass killing tied to Hungary's expulsion of 'foreign' Jews.

events.title: Hungarian forced labor service (Munkaszolgálat)
events.description: Before the 1944 deportations, tens of thousands of Hungarian Jewish men were conscripted into often deadly military labor battalions, many sent to the Eastern Front. A key fate for Hungarian Jewish men in this period.

events.title: Deportations to Transnistria
events.description: Romania deported Jews from Bessarabia, Bukovina, and elsewhere to camps and ghettos in Transnistria, where mass death from shootings, starvation, and disease followed.

events.title: Babi Yar massacre
events.description: Nearly 34,000 Jews of Kyiv were murdered over two days — among the largest single massacres of the Holocaust by shooting.

events.title: Theresienstadt ghetto-camp established
events.description: A walled garrison town used as a ghetto and transit camp, especially for Czech, German, and Austrian Jews, the elderly, and prominent figures. Most held there were later deported on to Auschwitz and other killing centers.

events.title: Wannsee Conference
events.description: Senior Nazi officials coordinate the 'Final Solution' — the systematic murder of European Jews.

events.title: Operation Reinhard begins (Bełżec, Sobibór, Treblinka)
events.description: The dedicated killing centers of Operation Reinhard begin operating, murdering most of Poland's Jews during 1942.

events.title: First deportation convoy from France to Auschwitz
events.description: The first major deportation convoy leaves France (via Drancy/Compiègne) for Auschwitz.

events.title: Vél' d'Hiv Roundup
events.description: French police arrest more than 13,000 Jews in Paris and hold them at the Vélodrome d'Hiver before deportation via Drancy.

events.title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
events.description: Armed Jewish resistance against deportations from the Warsaw Ghetto.

events.title: German occupation of Italy
events.description: After Italy's armistice with the Allies, Germany occupied the north and center. Systematic deportation of Italian Jews began — before this date, persecution was severe but deportations were limited. A crucial turning point for Italian cases.

events.title: Mass deportation of Hungarian Jews
events.description: Within about two months, roughly 440,000 Hungarian Jews are deported, mostly to Auschwitz.

events.title: Death marches
events.description: As the front lines closed in, the SS forced prisoners on brutal winter marches away from camps near the front; many died en route.

events.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
events.description: Soviet forces liberate Auschwitz-Birkenau.

events.title: Victory in Europe (VE Day)
events.description: Germany surrenders; the war in Europe ends. Survivors begin tracing relatives and the displaced-persons period begins.

events.title: Displaced Persons camps and emigration
events.description: Survivors lived in DP camps while seeking to emigrate, many to Israel (especially after 1948) or the United States. This period generated rich tracing, registration, and immigration records.
